light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a ranch hand with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the kitchen behind stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores and uneven tone; hair with stray curls; the denim shirt faded and creased, the leather apron scuffed. Food looks like real home cooking, not styled. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld video filmed by a ranch hand with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the kitchen in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and rough working hands; he moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: Claudio, a weathered 58-year-old Mexican-American ranch cook with curly black hair streaked with gray under a worn natural straw cowboy hat, a short gray-black beard and mustache, brown eyes, sun-tanned lined skin, wearing a faded blue denim work shirt with pearl snap buttons and the sleeves rolled to the forearms, a red bandana knotted at the neck and a worn brown leather apron stands at the wooden plank table; on a cutting board in front of him: a smoked ham hock, a large white onion, a head of garlic, two dried dark red ancho chiles, a small can of lard and a box of kosher salt. The place: the old cook house kitchen of a working cattle ranch: whitewashed adobe walls, heavy dark wooden ceiling beams, worn terracotta tile floor; a long scarred wooden plank table with a worn wooden cutting board, glass jars of dried beans and chiles, a clay jug, and behind it a deep window in the thick adobe wall looking out on a weathered wooden corral fence under the sun. Seen from a ranch hand's handheld camera at eye level, a medium shot from the waist up. clips.text: Back to the pot. While the beans rest, get your other things ready. One smoked ham hock. Or if you can't find one, four ounces of salt pork. One large white onion, cut in half. Don't chop it.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, holds up the smoked ham hock in one hand, then cuts the onion in half with a big knife. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: Just cut it in half, skin off. Four cloves of garlic, smashed with the side of your knife. Two dried chiles, ancho or guajillo, with the stems and seeds pulled out. Two tablespoons of lard or bacon grease.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, smashes a garlic clove with the flat side of the knife. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: And two teaspoons of kosher salt. The chiles aren't for heat. Ancho and guajillo are mild. They give the broth a deep red color and a little sweetness, like raisins.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, pulls the stem off a dried ancho chile and shakes the seeds out. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: You won't taste them as chile. You'll just taste better beans. If you've only got chili powder in a jar, use a teaspoon.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, holds up the dried chile toward the camera and smiles. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps.
